title: Implementation discipline
summary: Implementation MUST remain within the approved plan, establish exactly one deterministic pre-edit repository-check baseline per unit of work, run only blast-radius tests while iterating, leave the fast and integration suites to the gates, and directly remediate every cause of a retry.
instructions: Each material change MUST map to an acceptance criterion or an explicitly documented enabling change.
Agents MUST NOT redesign adjacent systems unless the approved plan requires it.

instructions.text: Before the first coder invocation of a unit of work, the harness MUST run and persist exactly one baseline for each interior gate profile. An interior gate profile is a profile other than full that a source-allowed stage gate references under the run's verification level. Under every built-in level the interior gate profiles are static and fast. The full profile MUST NOT run as a baseline. The baseline makes a pre-existing failure distinguishable from a regression. Coverage: `tests/integration/cohort-fanout-start.test.ts::a cohort captures one shared pre-implementation baseline that every chunk run adopts`.

A unit of work is one delivery run, or one cohort session together with every chunk run and the release run it starts. A cohort session MUST hold exactly one shared baseline per interior gate profile. The first run of the session that prepares a source-allowed stage captures it in its own worktree. That run records it on the cohort record under runtime/logs/cohorts/. Every other run of the session MUST adopt the recorded baseline and MUST NOT capture its own. Coverage: `tests/integration/cohort-baseline-concurrency.test.ts::three concurrent sibling prepares join one complete baseline collection`.

instructions: The coder MUST inspect the pre-implementation static and fast baselines before editing. The coder SHOULD repair existing failures when repair is bounded and low-risk. An unchanged pre-existing failure MUST NOT block the workflow when remediation would be broad, structural, or unrelated to the approved change. Any new or worsened diagnostic MUST remain a hard failure.

On a retry of the implementation stage, the coder MUST do work that directly addresses every issue causing the retry. The coder MUST populate implementation.remediation with cause, action, and evidence. A paperwork-only retry is prohibited.
The coder MUST NOT run the full profile or run the fast profile when an exit gate runs it.
Each added test MUST appear in tests_added with the contract it proves.
A worker MAY submit pending_harness only for shell criteria in its resolved invocation rubric. unevaluated remains an unfinished scaffold value and MUST NOT be submitted.

instructions.text: The harness MUST validate worker judgments, claims, read attestation, and blocking artifacts before executing gates. An eligible success MUST run each required gate once, subject to accepted recorded passes and explicit disables, and settle from deterministic evidence without another worker invocation. The harness MUST retain the original worker claims separately from deterministic results. A missing result or unauthorized skip MUST NOT satisfy a pending check. Selected test evidence MUST NOT become a profile pass. Coverage: `tests/integration/pending-harness-criteria.test.ts::merge patch pending criteria settle the same retry without another worker`.

instructions: On a retry that changed only output claims or evidence, the coder MUST NOT run any test profile. The retry MUST cite the evidence of the prior run.

instructions.text: The harness MUST rerun declared deterministic gates independently on any submission that can still succeed. The next instruction names the one exception: an accepted recorded pass. A non-success outcome is a declared failure or blocked result, a failed hard self-criterion, or a failed read attestation. When the submitted output already decides a non-success outcome, the harness MUST NOT run shell gate commands. The harness MUST record each affected gate as skipped with the deciding reason. Coverage: `tests/integration/pending-harness-criteria.test.ts::a failed required gate settles pending success as failure without rewriting the claim`.

The harness MAY accept a recorded clean pass of the identical gate command instead of re-executing it. Acceptance needs an unchanged Git workspace fingerprint, an unchanged repository-check configuration, a record under 24 hours old, and a resolved run baseline. The harness MUST mark an accepted pass as cached. An accepted pass MUST carry the original captured output as its evidence. An accepted pass MUST NOT be a failure, timeout, skip, override, or baseline-relative credit. PAN_GATE_CACHE=0 disables acceptance. Coverage: `tests/integration/gate-cache.test.ts::a clean gate pass is cached and accepted at an unchanged fingerprint`.

instructions: Before submission, the implementation record, changed-file claims, retry-remediation evidence, acceptance evidence, and referenced summary artifact MUST run their resolved policy-bound validators under VALID-001.

The fast/default profile MUST contain only deterministic offline tests. The coder MUST mark tests that make real external network or catalog calls, and MUST confine them to a secondary, integration, or full-only profile.

instructions.text: A repository-check gate MAY classify a new failing test as `environment_or_flake` only under three conditions. First, the test is outside the changed import closure. Second, the baseline did not fail that identity. Third, exactly one isolated rerun through the profile's reviewed `isolation_command` exits cleanly and reports the named test as run. The changed closure MUST come from the dirty working tree together with the paths the stage absorbed into a commit. When no change evidence exists at all, the gate MUST classify every failure as `isolation_unavailable` and MUST NOT reclassify. Coverage: `tests/integration/gate-failure-classification.test.ts::an out-of-closure failure that passes isolation becomes an advisory pass`.

A clean exit whose transcript does not name the test MUST classify as `isolation_unproven` and MUST fail the gate. A failure inside the closure, a second failure, an unparseable identity, or an absent isolation command MUST fail as before. The harness MUST record each classification, and its reason, in the deterministic gate result. `loadRepositoryChecks` validates that `isolation_command` contains `{file}` and either `{test_pattern}` or `{test}`. `{test_pattern}` receives the test name as an anchored regular expression, and `{test}` receives it literally. This instruction is the implementation specification until repository-check configuration becomes a policy-bound registry target. Coverage: `tests/integration/gate-failure-classification.test.ts::a clean isolation exit that names no test never earns a pass`.

Elapsed clock time alone MUST NOT fail a repository check that exits successfully. The harness MUST record a slow successful check as an operator FYI. A timeout, hang, nonzero exit, or new diagnostic remains actionable. Coverage: `tests/integration/fast-wall-cli.test.ts::a breached suite-cost advisory records run state and queues performance tuning`.

instructions: The coder SHOULD record `data.implementation.handoff` with where the next worker should start, the symbols it changed, its decisions, and what it left unproven. A later source-editing worker receives that handoff with the harness's reading map of the coder's transcript, and it SHOULD start from them instead of exploring the codebase again. This saves worker turns and context.

guidance_sources.read_trigger: Read this guidance before you run tests during implementation or remediation.
